title: Structure and magnetic properties of a 3d–4f CoIII2DyIII4 cluster

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, Co(OAc)2·4H2O (0.1248 g, 501 μmol) and Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.2283 g, 500 μmol) were dissolved in methanol (40.0 mL) and H2O (2.0 mL), followed by addition of 3-amino-1-propanol (0.0373 g, 497 μmol), salicylaldehyde (0.0609 g, 499 μmol) and Et3N (0.0506 g, 500 μmol). The orange solution was stirred for 1 h and filtered. Vapor diffusion of Et2O turned the filtrate yellow-green and afforded discrete green crystals after two days. Crystals were kept in contact with the mother liquor for X-ray crystallography. H2salpa (N-(2-hydroxybenzyl)-3-amino-1-propanol) is formed in situ from salicylaldehyde and 3-amino-1-propanol.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature (stirring); crystallization not otherwise specified
synthesis.time: stirred 1 h; crystals formed after two days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic solution reaction followed by Et2O vapor diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; vapor diffusion of Et2O into the filtrate yielded green crystals after two days; crystals maintained in mother liquor for crystallography

properties.summary: Because CoIII is diamagnetic, the magnetism of 1 arises from four DyIII ions in a planar Dy4 defect-dicubane core. DC χMT decreases from 54.29 cm3 mol−1 K at 300 K to 40.04 cm3 mol−1 K at 1.8 K, attributed mainly to thermal depopulation of DyIII Stark sublevels (possible weak antiferromagnetic exchange). Magnetization reaches 19.45 μB at 2 K and 70 kOe, below full saturation. AC susceptibility in zero DC field shows out-of-phase χM″ below 10 K (slow relaxation/SMM-like behavior) without maxima above 1.8 K; an approximate barrier of ~2 K and τ0 ~10−6 s were obtained from ln(χM″/χM′) vs 1/T.
